To simplify the fraction, multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator.

The conjugate of $2+\sqrt{3}$ is $2-\sqrt{3}$.  Therefore:

\begin{align*}
\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{3}} \cdot \frac{2-\sqrt{3}}{2-\sqrt{3}} &= \frac{(1+\sqrt{2})(2-\sqrt{3})}{(2+\sqrt{3})(2-\sqrt{3})} \\
&= \frac{2 - \sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}}{4 - 3} \\
&= (2 - \sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{6}) \\
&= A(1+\sqrt{B})-(\sqrt{C}+\sqrt{D})
\end{align*}

We can solve for the values of A, B, C, and D.
